title: Study of the circulation of dengue, yellow fever, and West Nile viruses in Guinea: implications for achieving the health objectives of the Simandou 2040 program

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the circulation of dengue virus (DENV), yellow fever virus (YFV), and West Nile virus (WNV) in Guinea, focusing on their prevalence in human and vector populations across the country's four ecological zones. The central question is to assess the serological evidence of exposure to these arboviruses and identify risk factors for infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a cross-sectional study conducted across 18 prefectures in Guinea from May to November 2024. Blood samples were collected from asymptomatic patients aged 1-90 years, and mosquitoes were collected using light traps. Serological testing was performed using ELISA, and mosquito samples were analyzed via real-time PCR. The study covered all four ecological zones of Guinea.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study confirms widespread serological evidence of exposure to DENV, YFV, and WNV across all ecological regions of Guinea. The highest seroprevalence of DENV was in N'Zerekore (43.9%), YFV in Kankan (54.7%), and WNV in Forecariah (53.0%). Adults, particularly farmers and livestock breeders, showed higher seropositivity for DENV and YFV. WNV was detected in Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes, suggesting its role in local transmission.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: No DENV or YFV infections were detected in vectors, despite human seropositivity, indicating gaps in understanding vector involvement for these viruses. The study does not address the absence of DENV/YFV in vectors or the potential for silent transmission cycles. Additionally, the lack of molecular confirmation for human infections beyond serology represents a methodological limitation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the need for an integrated arbovirus surveillance system in Guinea that combines serological surveillance with entomological surveys. This system is critical for supporting the public health objectives of the Simandou 2040 program. Targeted interventions should focus on high-risk groups such as farmers and livestock breeders.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides comprehensive evidence of dengue, yellow fever, and West Nile virus circulation in Guinea, with seroprevalence rates varying by region and occupation. While WNV was detected in Culex mosquitoes, the absence of DENV/YFV in vectors despite human infections warrants further investigation. The results underscore the need for integrated surveillance systems to guide public health interventions, particularly for high-risk adult populations involved in agriculture and livestock rearing.

title: Global molecular and serological evidence of dengue and chikungunya infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 158,608 tested participants.

analysis.scope_and_question: Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are Aedes-borne arboviruses with overlapping clinical manifestations, shared vectors, and substantial diagnostic challenges in co-endemic settings.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized published evidence on molecular detection, serological positivity, and DENV–CHIKV dual positivity/co-infection in human clinical, surveillance, and community-based study populations. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, five bibliographic databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar) and supplementary grey-literature/preprint sources were searched for English-language studies published from 1 January 1980 to 31 December 2024. Eligible records reported extractable numerators and denominators for DENV and/or CHIKV in humans using recognized molecular or serological assays.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled DENV estimate was 13.8 % (95 % CI: 10.9–17.3; I 2 =99.0 %), with molecular and serological estimates of 13.1 % (95 % CI: 7.9–21.0) and 14.3 % (95 % CI: 10.2–19.8), respectively. The pooled CHIKV estimate was 14.0 % (95 % CI: 12.0–16.4; I 2 =97.5 %), with molecular and serological estimates of 9.8 and 15.7 %, respectively. DENV–CHIKV dual positivity/co-infection was 52.9 % (95 % CI: 48.7–57.1) among studies that tested and reported both outcomes. Available evidence indicates extensive but highly heterogeneous DENV and CHIKV positivity across selected clinical and surveillance populations.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The pooled estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial between-study heterogeneity, diagnostic variability, outbreak-period sampling, and uneven geographic representation. Country-level estimates varied widely and should be interpreted as summaries of available studies rather than nationally representative burden estimates. Funnel-plot asymmetry was statistically significant in DENV analyses but not in the overall CHIKV analysis. No prospective PROSPERO or OSF protocol registration was available.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings support integrated arboviral surveillance, multiplex diagnostics, and vector-control preparedness in co-endemic regions.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized molecular and serological evidence of dengue (DENV) and chikungunya (CHIKV) infections across 196 studies involving 158,608 participants. Pooled estimates showed DENV positivity at 13.8% (95% CI: 10.9–17.3) and CHIKV at 14.0% (95% CI: 12.0–16.4), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 >97%). Dual positivity reached 52.9% in co-endemic settings. Country-level estimates varied widely, reflecting diagnostic variability and uneven geographic representation. The findings underscore the need for integrated arboviral surveillance, multiplex diagnostics, and vector-control preparedness in regions where these viruses co-circulate.

title: Economic Impact of Dengue Virus in Mexico Over One Decade: A Systematic Literature Review (2010–2020)

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the economic impact of dengue virus in Mexico over the decade 2010–2020, focusing on direct and indirect costs associated with care, prevention, and surveillance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic literature review was conducted using Embase, MEDLINE, Evidence-Based Medicine Reviews, SciELO, and LILACS, with additional review of grey literature and National Ministry of Health reports. Studies published in English or Spanish between 2010–2020 were assessed using the PICOS framework and the National Health Service Wales tool for quality.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The economic burden of dengue in Mexico is substantial, peaking in 2013 with annual costs of $176.82 million (adjusted present value: $281.60 million). All included studies reported nationwide costs, with three focusing on specific Mexican states.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Heterogeneity in methodological approaches among cost studies challenges direct comparison, and the review does not address regional variations beyond the three specific states mentioned.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to standardize cost methodologies and explore regional economic impacts. Surveillance and outbreak response strategies should be optimized to mitigate healthcare system costs and productivity losses.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review evaluates the economic impact of dengue virus in Mexico from 2010–2020, analyzing direct and indirect costs. Seven studies met inclusion criteria, reporting substantial nationwide costs peaking at $176.82 million in 2013. Methodological heterogeneity complicates comparisons, and regional data is limited. The findings highlight significant healthcare and productivity burdens, emphasizing the need for standardized cost assessments and improved outbreak management strategies.

title: Design of a novel epitope-based tetravalent subunit vaccine against dengue virus: An immunoinformatic approach

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue imposes a profound global impact, with millions affected annually, and despite efforts, no impeccable antiviral treatment exists to date, highlighting the urgency for a vaccine.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study employed an immunoinformatics approach to design an epitope-based tetravalent subunit vaccine aimed at confronting all DENV serotypes, with no specific population or clinical cohort involved.
analysis.methods: The study involved epitope prediction and screening, physicochemical assessment, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, immune simulations, and in silico cloning to evaluate the vaccine construct.
analysis.main_results: The vaccine construct showed an antigenicity of 0.9319 with 97.35% population coverage worldwide; molecular docking with TLR2 and TLR4 revealed promising interactions with lowest energies of −1240.5 kJ/mol and −1393.3 kJ/mol, respectively, and MD simulations confirmed stability and flexibility.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the vaccine outperforms any other Dengue vaccine developed to date, as evidenced by its robust immune response and high antigenicity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest potential for improved dengue prevention through a tetravalent subunit vaccine with broad population coverage and strong immune stimulation, though further validation is needed.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is limited because the study was conducted entirely through in silico methods, and in vitro and in vivo validations are required to confirm the vaccine as a potential candidate for clinical trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study designed a novel epitope-based tetravalent subunit vaccine against dengue virus using an immunoinformatics approach. The vaccine includes human β-defensin 3 adjuvant and 23 epitopes, showing high antigenicity (0.9319) and 97.35% global population coverage. Molecular docking revealed strong interactions with TLR2 and TLR4, and MD simulations confirmed stability. The vaccine elicited robust immune responses with high-titer antibodies and pro-inflammatory cytokines. However, as the study was entirely computational, in vitro and in vivo validations are necessary before clinical trials.

title: Comparative Performance of Mechanistic, Statistical, and Hybrid Models of Forecasting Dengue Fever Incidence in Somalia. A Retrospective Time Series Analysis

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue fever is a growing menace in Somalia, a climate change prone region with a weak healthcare system, and this study aimed to find the best forecasting model for dengue fever in this data-sparse situation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective time series analysis utilized raw reported annual incidence data of dengue from 1990 to 2021 (N = 32) obtained from Our World in Data.
analysis.methods: We tested a mechanistic Susceptible-Infected-Recovered (SIR) model, 8 single time series models (ARIMA, ETS, TBATS, and NNAR), and 12 hybrids using an averaging ensemble strategy, with data divided into training (1990–2016) and testing (2017–2021) sets.
analysis.main_results: The hybrid ARIMA-TBATS model was the most successful, with a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 6.49% and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 663.81, outperforming the best single model (TBATS) which had a MAPE of 7.14%; the SIR model calculated a basic reproduction number (R0) of 1.015, indicating endemic disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that the ARIMA-TBATS hybrid is the most empirically effective tool for forecasting dengue in Somalia, representing a novel approach tailored to data-sparse settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This ARIMA-TBATS framework is designed to serve as the mathematical engine for a National Dengue Early Warning System (DEWS) in Somalia, enabling public health officials to preempt outbreaks by routing medical supplies, mobilizing fumigation teams, and distributing bed nets to high-risk zones months before peak incidence occurs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Due to the lack of standardized case definitions and high under-reporting inherent to Somalia's surveillance system, forecasts represent the projected reported burden rather than true infection rates; the evidence strength is moderate given the retrospective design and reliance on reported data.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared mechanistic, statistical, and hybrid models for forecasting dengue fever incidence in Somalia using annual data from 1990–2021. The hybrid ARIMA-TBATS model outperformed all others, achieving a MAPE of 6.49% and RMSE of 663.81, while the SIR model indicated endemic disease (R0 = 1.015). The authors recommend this hybrid model for a National Dengue Early Warning System to enable early outbreak response, though forecasts reflect reported burden rather than true infection rates due to surveillance limitations.

title: Antibody Responses in Pediatric Dengue Indicate Emergence and Co‐Circulation of DENV‐3 Genotypes I and III in Myanmar and Orthoflavivirus Cross‐Reactivity

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus (DENV) remains a major public health concern in Southeast Asia, disproportionately affecting children. The study aimed to understand the immunological implications of the emergence of DENV-3 Genotype I in Myanmar.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed paired acute and convalescent serum samples from 38 pediatric dengue patients collected between 2017 and 2019, alongside archived 2004 samples. It focused on DENV-3 Genotypes I and III and their impact on antibody responses in Myanmar.
analysis.methods: To assess the impact of the emergence of DENV-3 Genotype I, neutralization and in vitro antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) were evaluated against DENV-3 Genotypes I and III and other serotypes. Cross-reactivity with Zika and Japanese encephalitis viruses was also analyzed.
analysis.main_results: Samples from 2004 showed reduced neutralization and higher ADE for Genotype I, consistent with its absence at the time. In contrast, 2017–2019 samples exhibited comparable neutralization for both genotypes, with genotype- and year-dependent ADE differences.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that the emergence of Genotype I was associated with evolving functional antibody profiles. This provides immunological evidence for the continued co-circulation of DENV-3 Genotypes I and III in Myanmar.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results contribute to understanding how antibody responses evolve with the emergence of new DENV-3 genotypes, which is critical for surveillance and vaccine development in endemic regions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on archived samples. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on cross-sectional analysis of antibody profiles rather than longitudinal or experimental data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the emergence and co-circulation of DENV-3 Genotypes I and III in Myanmar by analyzing antibody responses in pediatric dengue patients. Using paired serum samples from 2004 and 2017–2019, the researchers assessed neutralization and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) against these genotypes and other serotypes, as well as cross-reactivity with Zika and Japanese encephalitis viruses. Results showed that 2004 samples had reduced neutralization and higher ADE for Genotype I, consistent with its absence at the time, while 2017–2019 samples exhibited comparable neutralization for both genotypes, with genotype- and year-dependent ADE differences. These findings suggest evolving functional antibody profiles associated with the emergence of Genotype I and provide immunological evidence for its continued co-circulation with Genotype III in Myanmar. The study's limitations include its retrospective design and reliance on archived samples, which may affect the strength of the evidence. The results have implications for understanding how pre-existing immunity influences genotype dynamics and cross-reactivity in dengue-endemic regions.

title: Immune Modulatory Therapy for Severe Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever in a Patient With Mitochondrial Complex I Deficiency: A Case Report

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue virus (DENV) poses a serious global health challenge, particularly in cases of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF). Patients with preexisting mitochondrial disorders may be at increased risk for complications due to the specific impact of DENV on mitochondrial‐dependent cellular processes and immune function.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We describe a 16‐year‐old male with known mitochondrial complex I deficiency caused by a homozygous likely pathogenic variant in NDUFV1 who subsequently developed DHF.
analysis.methods: His clinical course was further complicated by encephalitis, arachnoiditis, and myelitis requiring extensive immunomodulation. He received corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and plasma exchange (PLEX), which led to improvement and partial recovery of functional status.
analysis.main_results: His illness was marked by rapidly worsening weakness, respiratory distress, intracranial hemorrhage, and seizures.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This case highlights several rare complications of dengue fever, the impact of DENV on mitochondrial function, and underscores the complexity of managing infectious diseases in individuals with underlying mitochondrial disorders.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for heightened awareness and tailored management strategies for dengue patients with mitochondrial disorders, emphasizing the role of immunomodulatory therapy in severe cases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on a single case report, limiting generalizability, but provides detailed clinical insights into a rare complication of dengue in a patient with mitochondrial complex I deficiency.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 16-year-old male with mitochondrial complex I deficiency who developed dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF). His illness was marked by severe complications including weakness, respiratory distress, intracranial hemorrhage, seizures, encephalitis, arachnoiditis, and myelitis. The patient received immunomodulatory therapy with corticosteroids, IVIG, and plasma exchange, leading to partial recovery. The case highlights the impact of DENV on mitochondrial function and underscores the complexity of managing dengue in patients with underlying mitochondrial disorders, suggesting the need for tailored therapeutic approaches.

title: Characterization of vaccine viremia, attenuation reversion, and safety: Combined results from the TAK-003 dengue vaccine clinical development program.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the presence of vaccine RNAemia, attenuation loci reversions, and their association with viral-syndrome-like adverse events in participants throughout the TAK-003 dengue vaccine clinical development program, addressing concerns about live-attenuated vaccines potentially causing transient symptoms resembling natural infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The analysis included pooled phase 1/2 trial data and participants from the pivotal phase 3 DEN-301 trial and phase 2 DEN-313 trial who experienced febrile illness within 30 days post-vaccination, with TAK-003 RNA-positive serum samples evaluated for viral replication and sequenced for reversions.
analysis.methods: Safety data (solicited adverse events within 7/14 days; unsolicited adverse events within 28 days) were assessed from pooled phase 1/2 trials, and participants with febrile illness in DEN-301/DEN-313 trials were tested for RNAemia and evaluated for adverse events.
analysis.main_results: TAK-003 RNAemia was detected in 441/805 (54.8%) of vaccinees, peaking during the second week post-vaccination and mostly occurring after the first dose, with DENV-2 being the most common component detected; 69 single locus reversions were found, and adverse events in participants with reversions were generally non-serious.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that RNAemia was associated with transient, mild-to-moderate symptoms resembling natural infection, which were also observed in the absence of RNAemia, demonstrating that attenuation reversions did not indicate increased symptom severity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform that TAK-003 vaccine viremia is common but generally mild, supporting its safety profile and aiding in distinguishing vaccine-related symptoms from natural dengue infection in surveillance and clinical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on pooled trial data and observational analysis of febrile illness cases, which may introduce selection bias, though the large sample size and comprehensive sequencing enhance reliability.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized vaccine viremia, attenuation reversion, and safety of the TAK-003 dengue vaccine across its clinical development program. RNAemia was detected in 54.8% of vaccinees, peaking in the second week post-vaccination and predominantly involving DENV-2. While 69 single locus reversions occurred, they were not associated with increased symptom severity. RNAemia was linked to transient, mild-to-moderate symptoms resembling natural infection, though similar symptoms were also seen without RNAemia. Common adverse events included injection site pain and headache, with higher incidences in RNAemic participants. The findings support the vaccine's safety profile and aid in distinguishing vaccine-related effects from natural dengue infection.

title: Computational insights into dengue virus envelope protein triggered membrane fusion process

analysis.research_question_and_background: The membrane fusion process initiated by the Envelope (E) protein of the Dengue virus (DENV) is a critical step in viral entry into host cells, yet its molecular mechanism remains only partially understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors employed a combination of all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the insertion and progression of the dengue virus Envelope protein into a lipid bilayer, capturing key stages of the membrane fusion event.
analysis.methods: All-atom simulations provided atomistic insight into initial protein‐lipid interactions, time evolution of protein‐lipid contacts and conformational rearrangements of the E protein fusion loop, while coarse‐grained models enabled observation of long‐timescale membrane remodeling events such as curvature generation.
analysis.main_results: Structural and dynamic analyses revealed how the E protein perturbs membrane architecture, promoting negative curvature at the entry site and positive curvature in adjoining regions that resemble early hemifusion intermediates.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings support the hypothesis that the fusion loop acts as a membrane anchor and that coordinated protein insertion and tilting are essential for catalyzing membrane merger, offering a novel mechanistic view of dengue virus fusion initiation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides a detailed molecular view of dengue virus fusion initiation and demonstrates the value of multiscale simulation approaches for investigating complex membrane‐protein interactions, informing future therapeutic targeting of the fusion process.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report any limitations or an assessment of evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: Dengue virus entry relies on membrane fusion mediated by the Envelope (E) protein, a process whose molecular details are incompletely understood. To address this gap, the researchers used both all‐atom and coarse‐grained molecular dynamics simulations to model how the E protein inserts into and remodels a lipid bilayer. The simulations showed that the protein induces negative curvature at the site of entry and positive curvature in surrounding areas, forming structures reminiscent of early hemifusion intermediates. These observations support the idea that the fusion loop serves as a membrane anchor and that coordinated insertion and tilting of the protein are crucial for membrane merger. By delivering a high‐resolution, multiscale view of the fusion mechanism, the work highlights the utility of computational approaches for elucidating viral entry and may guide future antiviral strategies targeting this step.

title: Substance P and NK‐1R in Dengue: A First Serological Investigation

title: Dengue virus 2 vector competence in heatwave-exposed Aedes aegypti mosquitoes is reduced by 5-methylcytosine RNA disruption

analysis.research_question_and_background: Extreme weather events can profoundly alter the transmission dynamics of dengue virus (DENV) by its primary vector, Aedes aegypti. Understanding how mosquitoes respond to heat stress and how this affects viral transmission is critical for informing global public health strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the effects of a 5-day heatwave on Aedes aegypti mosquitoes infected with DENV2, examining changes in lifespan, viral transmission potential, and RNA methylation levels.
analysis.methods: Researchers exposed mosquitoes to a heatwave at the time of DENV2 acquisition and measured global 5-methylcytosine RNA (5mC-RNA) levels, antiviral gene expression, and viral replication. Pharmacological disruption of 5mC-RNA was performed using azacytidine to assess its impact on transmission potential.
analysis.main_results: Heatwave-exposed mosquitoes exhibited elevated global 5mC-RNA levels and suppressed antiviral gene expression, facilitating efficient viral replication. Pharmacological disruption of 5mC-RNA reduced DENV2 infection prevalence from 78% to 37% and restored mosquito late-life survival to rates comparable to non-stressed controls.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that heatwaves amplify dengue transmission risk through an epitranscriptomic mechanism involving RNA methylation, which suppresses antiviral responses. This study highlights RNA methylation as a potential target for mitigating DENV transmission under climate stress.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting RNA methylation could be a novel strategy to reduce dengue transmission during heatwaves, informing surveillance and intervention programs in regions facing climate extremes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study demonstrates a strong mechanistic link between heat stress, RNA methylation, and dengue transmission, but further research is needed to validate these findings in field settings and assess long-term ecological impacts.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how heatwaves affect dengue virus (DENV2) transmission in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. The researchers found that a 5-day heatwave increases mosquito lifespan and viral replication by elevating 5-methylcytosine RNA (5mC-RNA) levels and suppressing antiviral gene expression. Pharmacological disruption of 5mC-RNA with azacytidine reduced infection prevalence from 78% to 37% and restored survival rates. The study reveals an epitranscriptomic mechanism by which heatwaves amplify dengue risk and suggests RNA methylation as a potential target for transmission control.

title: Uncovering dengue serotype-specific transmission, cross-reactivity, and immune profiles from cross-sectional serosurveys

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on dengue virus (DENV-1 to DENV-4) and its transmission, cross-reactivity, and immune profiles using cross-sectional serosurveys. The central question is how to infer serotype-specific force of infection (FOI) and cross-reactivity from cross-sectional data, addressing limitations in traditional methods.

title: Immature platelet fraction predicts differential platelet recovery trajectories in dengue fever: A longitudinal analysis

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue commonly causes thrombocytopenia, but platelet count alone may not reflect marrow thrombopoiesis. analysis.methods: Log‐transformed platelet counts at Day 3 and Day 5 were analysed using generalized least squares regression. Longitudinal changes were assessed using the Friedman test.
analysis.main_results: Platelet counts declined from 118 to 98 × 10 9 /L ( p = 0.0017), while IPF increased from 9.7% to 12.9% ( p < 0.0001). analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that IPF is a dynamic biomarker that predicts platelet recovery trajectory in dengue.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was retrospective and based on data from a single tertiary care hospital, which may limit generalisability. The evidence is moderate as it is based on observational data without randomization or control groups.

title: XPO1-dependent nuclear export regulates NS3 localization and promotes DENV-2 replication through mitochondrial remodeling and interferon suppression

However, the study is limited to in vitro experiments, which may not fully capture in vivo dynamics, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: A tiered molecular surveillance framework linking rapid dengue detection to genomic epidemiology in Senegal.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Arboviral surveillance in Africa is limited by fragmented diagnostic capacity and insufficient integration of molecular detection with genomic epidemiology, particularly in settings where dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), and chikungunya (CHIKV) viruses co-circulate and present with overlapping clinical syndromes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a molecular surveillance study across multiple regions in Senegal, including samples collected from 367 individuals with febrile or non-febrile illness.
analysis.methods: A tiered workflow was implemented using multiplex reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) screening for DENV, ZIKV, and CHIKV, performed on a combination of individually tested samples (n=43) and pooled samples (three individuals per pool). DENV RT-qPCR-positive samples were further characterized by reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification (RT-RPA) serotyping and genomic sequencing.
analysis.main_results: Multiplex RT-qPCR revealed concurrent circulation of multiple arboviruses. Among individually tested samples, positivity rates were 20·9% (9/43) for DENV, 9·3% (4/43) for ZIKV, and 11·6% (5/43) for CHIKV. In pooled screening across all sites (108 pools), positivity rates were 18·5% for DENV (20/108), 5·6% for ZIKV (6/108), and 10·2% for CHIKV (11/108), indicating widespread arboviral transmission.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings demonstrate co-circulation of DENV, ZIKV, and CHIKV in Senegal and provide evidence of recent expansion of DENV-2 within a globally connected transmission network.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide evidence of recent emergence and rapid expansion of DENV-2, which can inform targeted surveillance, diagnosis, and public health interventions in Senegal and other regions with similar arboviral dynamics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A tiered strategy integrating pooled molecular screening with RT-RPA triage and genomic sequencing offers a scalable framework for arboviral surveillance in resource-limited settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a tiered molecular surveillance framework for arboviruses in Senegal, focusing on dengue virus (DENV) and its co-circulation with Zika (ZIKV) and chikungunya (CHIKV) viruses. The research aimed to address the limitations of fragmented diagnostic capacity and the lack of integration between molecular detection and genomic epidemiology in Africa. A combination of multiplex RT-qPCR screening, RT-RPA serotyping, and genomic sequencing was used to analyze 367 samples, revealing concurrent circulation of DENV, ZIKV, and CHIKV. Positivity rates for DENV were higher than for ZIKV and CHIKV in both individually tested and pooled samples, indicating widespread transmission. The results showed that all DENV-2 sequences clustered within the cosmopolitan genotype II, lineage II-F.1.1, and were closely related to recent strains from West Africa and Asia. These findings suggest recent emergence and rapid expansion of DENV-2 within a globally connected transmission network, highlighting the need for improved surveillance strategies. The study's tiered approach, which combines pooled screening with RT-RPA triage and genomic sequencing, offers a scalable framework for arboviral surveillance in resource-limited settings.

title: Broadly cross-reactive neutralizing and enhancing antibody responses to dengue, Japanese encephalitis viruses and Zika in sera from Vietnamese pediatric dengue cases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Understanding the balance between protective and pathogenic antibody responses is central to dengue immunology and flavivirus vaccine development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Fifty paired acute and convalescent serum samples from pediatric dengue patients in southern Vietnam (2015-2017) were analyzed, including primary and secondary infections across a spectrum of disease severity.
analysis.methods: Primary and secondary DENV infections were classified using an in-house validated DENV IgG ELISA. Neutralizing antibody (NAb) titers and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) activities were evaluated against dengue virus the four serotypes (DENV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) and ZIKA (ZIKV) using single-round infectious particles (SRIPs).
analysis.main_results: Neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses were detected against all DENV serotypes and were highest against DENV-1. NAb titers increased during convalescence and were generally higher in secondary than primary infections. Higher NAb titers were also observed in convalescent sera from DSS cases compared with other clinical groups. ADE activity was most pronounced against DENV-2 and was lowest against DENV-4, while Peak enhancement titers (PET) were higher in convalescent samples, secondary infections, and DSS cases, and were positively correlated with NAb titers. Higher enhancement activity was observed in sera from DSS cases than in those from milder disease categories.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Heightened neutralizing immunity in secondary and severe dengue is accompanied by expanded enhancement potential, indicating an expanded, cross-reactive immune response driven by immune activation upon infection. The coexistence of protective and enhancing antibodies may contribute both to viral control and to immunopathogenesis during subsequent flavivirus infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of more effective dengue vaccines and highlight the importance of monitoring antibody responses in patients with severe dengue to better understand immunopathogenesis and improve treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to serum samples from pediatric dengue patients in southern Vietnam, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate as it is based on an abstract-only analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the balance between neutralizing and enhancing antibody responses in pediatric dengue patients in southern Vietnam. It analyzes 50 paired serum samples from 2015-2017, including primary and secondary infections across varying disease severities. The research employs an in-house validated DENV IgG ELISA to classify infections and evaluates neutralizing antibody (NAb) titers and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) activities against DENV serotypes, Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and Zika virus (ZIKV) using single-round infectious particles (SRIPs). The results show that NAb responses are highest against DENV-1 and increase during convalescence, with secondary infections and severe dengue cases exhibiting higher titers. ADE activity is most pronounced against DENV-2 and lowest against DENV-4, with peak enhancement titers (PET) correlating with NAb levels. Sera from severe dengue cases (DSS) demonstrate higher enhancement activity compared to milder cases. Cross-reactive antibodies against JEV and ZIKV are also detected, with stronger enhancement observed against ZIKV. The authors conclude that heightened neutralizing immunity in secondary and severe dengue is associated with expanded enhancement potential, suggesting an activated immune response. They also propose that the coexistence of protective and enhancing antibodies may influence both viral control and immunopathogenesis during subsequent flavivirus infections. The study's findings may contribute to the development of more effective dengue vaccines and improve understanding of immune responses in severe cases. However, the study is limited to a specific geographic and demographic population, which may affect generalizability, and the evidence is based on abstract-only data, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with dengue fever serotypes in Eastern Sudan: a hospital-based cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue is a critical public health threat in Sudan, exacerbated by rapid urbanization and climatic factors. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of dengue virus (DENV) serotypes and identify sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with specific serotypes among residents and internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Kassala during the 2024 epidemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at Kassala Teaching Hospital (October–December 2024). Among the confirmed 227 dengue fever cases, 52% of patients were IDPs, and 30.4% presented with severe forms (DHF/DSS).
analysis.methods: Serum samples from 227 confirmed dengue patients (RDT-positive for NS1, IgM, or both) were analyzed using one-step Real-Time PCR for serotyping. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with the most prevalent serotypes.
analysis.main_results: Among the confirmed 227 dengue fever cases, DENV-2 was the dominant serotype (59.9%), followed by DENV-3 (35.2%) and DENV-1 (4.8%). The overall mortality rate was 6.6%, with 13 out of the 15 recorded deaths occurring among the displaced population. Multivariate analysis revealed that the non-use of mosquito nets was the only independent factor associated with DENV-2 infection (adjusted odds ratio, AOR = 2.20; 95% CI: 1.23–3.90; P = 0.007).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The 2024 dengue outbreak marked a significant shift from DENV-3 to DENV-2 dominance, with a high mortality burden clustering heavily within vulnerable IDPs due to systemic displacement factors rather than strain dominance. The strong association between net non-use and DENV-2 highlights the urgent need for targeted long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) distribution and vector control in displacement camps.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The high fatality rate in the small DENV-1 subset underscores the necessity of strengthened molecular surveillance to monitor virulent strains in conflict zones. Additionally, the findings emphasize the need for targeted vector control measures to reduce dengue transmission in high-risk populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The high fatality rate among the small subset of DENV-1 patients must be interpreted with extreme caution due to the limited sample size. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study provides valuable insights into serotype prevalence and associated factors but is limited by its cross-sectional design and small sample size for certain serotypes.

analysis.summary_en: This hospital-based cross-sectional study in Kassala, Sudan, during the 2024 dengue outbreak aimed to determine DENV serotype prevalence and associated factors. Among 227 confirmed cases, DENV-2 was dominant (59.9%), followed by DENV-3 (35.2%) and DENV-1 (4.8%). The overall mortality rate was 6.6%, with 13 deaths among displaced persons. Non-use of mosquito nets was independently associated with DENV-2 infection (AOR = 2.20; P = 0.007). The outbreak marked a shift from DENV-3 to DENV-2 dominance, with high mortality clustering in IDPs. The findings highlight the need for targeted vector control and molecular surveillance in conflict zones.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the need for effective dengue management by proposing an optimal control framework that incorporates three key interventions: information-induced self-protection, saturated treatment, and pesticide use for vector control. The research evaluates seven distinct control policies through numerical simulations, demonstrating that the combined strategy of all controls is the most effective, reducing infection prevalence to minimal levels within approximately 60 days and maintaining sustained control. title: Dengue outbreak investigation in Mfandena I Health Area, Cameroon, 2025: Evidence of Aedes vectors and routine surveillance gaps

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focused on dengue virus outbreak investigation in Mfandena I Health Area, Cameroon, in 2025, with the central question being to identify evidence of Aedes vectors and evaluate routine surveillance gaps.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A cross-sectional study was conducted in January 2025 (dry season) in Mfandena I Health Area. Cases were identified through healthcare records reviews and community screening, with suspected cases defined by fever >38.5°C lasting 2-7 days and specific symptoms. Immunoglobulin M (IgM) and non-structural protein 1 (NS1) tests were performed, and an entomological survey was conducted within a 1 km radius around case residences.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The investigation confirmed 46 dengue cases (44 suspected, 2 confirmed) and identified Aedes albopictus as the primary vector (88% of collected mosquitoes). A discarded tyre containing Ae. albopictus larvae was identified as the likely infection source. The surveillance system exhibited significant gaps, with only 16% of staff familiar with case definitions and no notification forms available.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The surveillance system was found to be neither simple, acceptable, nor stable, with gaps in detection and reporting. No additional cases were confirmed among contacts, and the study was limited to the dry season, potentially missing seasonal variations in transmission or vector activity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Strengthening surveillance capacity and reinforcing routine entomological investigations are essential to improve outbreak detection, response, and prevention. The study highlights the need for better staff training on case definitions and improved notification systems.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated a dengue outbreak in Mfandena I Health Area, Cameroon, in 2025, identifying 46 cases and confirming Aedes albopictus as the primary vector. The investigation revealed significant gaps in the surveillance system, including poor staff familiarity with case definitions and lack of notification forms. The findings emphasize the need to strengthen surveillance capacity and routine entomological investigations to improve outbreak detection and response. The study was conducted during the dry season, which may limit the generalizability of findings to other seasons.

title: Knowledge–Practice Gap, Attitudes, and Determinants of Dengue Management Practices Among Physicians in Sudan: A Cross-Sectional Study, 2026

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue fever is an emerging public health threat in Sudan, where recurrent outbreaks occur within a fragile and conflict-affected health system, and limited evidence exists regarding whether dengue-related knowledge translates into appropriate clinical practice.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An online cross-sectional survey was conducted among physicians practicing in Sudan between February and April 2026.
analysis.methods: A structured questionnaire adapted from a validated dengue knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) instrument was used to collect data, and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with high dengue management practice.
analysis.main_results: A total of 633 physicians participated; only 3.8% demonstrated high disease knowledge, 28.8% had high vector knowledge, and 40.0% achieved high practice scores; only 36.2% reported familiarity with WHO dengue guidelines, and 57.7% reported inadequate resources.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A substantial knowledge–practice gap exists among physicians managing dengue in Sudan, and clinical practice was influenced more strongly by guideline familiarity, perceived guideline usefulness, and attitudes than by disease knowledge alone.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Strengthening physician preparedness through practical training, implementation of WHO dengue guidelines, and improved health-system readiness may enhance dengue management in conflict-affected settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data; evidence strength is moderate due to the large sample size but potential for recall bias and lack of objective practice assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed dengue-related knowledge, attitudes, practices, and clinical readiness among 633 physicians in Sudan in 2026. Findings revealed a significant knowledge–practice gap, with only 3.8% having high disease knowledge and 40% achieving high practice scores. Weak correlations between knowledge and practice (r = 0.077 for disease knowledge, r = 0.026 for vector knowledge) underscored this gap. Familiarity with WHO guidelines (AOR = 2.66), belief in their usefulness (AOR = 4.06), and higher attitude scores (AOR = 1.07) were independently associated with better practices, while disease knowledge was not. The study highlights the need for practical training, guideline implementation, and improved health-system resources to enhance dengue management in conflict-affected settings.

title: Dengue Fever Unmasking JAK2 Mutation-Related Polycythemia Vera Presenting With Extensive Splanchnic Venous Thrombosis and Hemorrhagic Complications: A Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenge

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue fever is a common arboviral infection characterized by fever, thrombocytopenia, and hemorrhagic manifestations, whereas thrombotic complications are relatively uncommon. This study reports a case of severe dengue infection revealing previously undiagnosed JAK2-related polycythemia vera (PV) complicated by extensive splanchnic venous thrombosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study reports a case of a 58-year-old male patient with a history of diabetes mellitus and hypertension who presented with a five-day history of fever, anorexia, and abdominal pain.
analysis.methods: Initial laboratory investigations demonstrated progressive thrombocytopenia, elevated hemoglobin, and increased hematocrit. Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis revealed extensive splanchnic venous thrombosis involving the superior mesenteric, splenic, and portal venous systems, along with acute pancreatitis.
analysis.main_results: During hospitalization, platelet counts continued to decline, and dengue serology returned positive. Further evaluation revealed splenomegaly and a positive JAK2 V617F mutation, confirming underlying polycythemia vera.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The patient subsequently developed mucosal bleeding and was treated with anticoagulation and hydroxyurea, resulting in clinical recovery. This case highlights the rare coexistence of hemorrhagic and thrombotic complications in dengue fever and emphasizes the importance of considering underlying myeloproliferative neoplasms in patients presenting with atypical thrombosis, erythrocytosis, or splenomegaly.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the need for vigilant monitoring and early diagnosis of underlying myeloproliferative disorders in patients with dengue fever to prevent severe complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-case nature, which may not be generalizable to a broader population. Using ecological data from 645 municipalities in São Paulo, Brazil, between January and June 2024, the research found that 16.7% of municipalities showed under-reporting, ranging from 1% to 95%, with an estimated 8,624 undetected cases. No significant associations were found between under-reporting and factors like health coverage or urbanization, but spatial analysis identified clusters in the northwestern region. The methodology can help identify areas with under-reporting and guide interventions, though comparisons between groups should be interpreted cautiously due to potential differences in risk and diagnostic criteria.

title: Household Characteristics, Residents’ Behaviors, and Seasonal Factors Associated With the Presence and Persistence of Aedes aegypti in a Dengue-Endemic Area

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the association between household characteristics, residents' preventive behaviors, seasonal factors, and the presence and persistence of Aedes aegypti in a dengue-endemic area. analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective cohort study was conducted in San Pedro Pochutla, Oaxaca, Mexico. A total of 68 inhabited dwellings were selected and characterized on a single occasion according to their structure, degree of marginalization, vulnerability, and environment.

The characteristics of the dwelling that represented a risk for the presence and persistence of Aedes aegypti were the lack of mosquito nets on doors, lack of pavilions on beds, animals in the household, and not applying insecticide indoors.
analysis.main_results: A total of 476 visits were conducted, identifying 494 breeding sites positive for Aedes aegypti larvae or pupae. A total of 48.5% of the homes studied were positive on at least two occasions, with marked temporal variation, particularly during the rainy season (67.7%). Most breeding sites were located outdoors (96%), predominantly in controllable containers (73%). The most important habitats were drums, barrels/sinks/tubs/pools, cans/buckets, tires, and kitchen/washing utensils (72.8%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Household conditions, human behavior, and seasonal variation significantly influence the presence and persistence of Aedes aegypti. These findings can inform targeted vector control strategies, particularly focusing on modifiable risk factors and seasonal interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: They provide insights into the environmental and behavioral factors that contribute to the persistence of Aedes aegypti in dengue-endemic areas.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a single location, which may limit generalizability. The evidence is strong as it is based on direct observations of breeding sites and associations with household and behavioral factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between household characteristics, residents' behaviors, and seasonal factors with the presence and persistence of Aedes aegypti in a dengue-endemic area. Conducted in San Pedro Pochutla, Oaxaca, Mexico, the prospective cohort study evaluated 68 dwellings over 12 months, performing seven entomological assessments. Most breeding sites were outdoors, with controllable containers being the most common. Key habitats included drums, barrels, cans, tires, and kitchen utensils. The study concluded that household conditions, human behavior, and seasonal variation significantly influence Aedes aegypti presence. These findings can guide targeted vector control strategies by highlighting modifiable risk factors and seasonal patterns. The evidence is strong due to direct observations, but the study's single-location focus may limit generalizability.

title: Characterization of Non-Neutralizing Antibody Responses in a Dengue Virus-4 Human Challenge Model 2243013

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the role of non-neutralizing antibodies (nNAbs) in dengue virus infection, as neutralizing antibody titers do not reliably predict disease outcomes, and the function of nNAbs remains poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In a phase 1 open-label study, 14 dengue-naïve subjects were subcutaneously inoculated with a slightly attenuated, live DENV-4 strain, H-241.
analysis.methods: Plasma was collected from pre- and 6 months post-infection to measure Ab-dependent complement deposition, Ab-dependent cellular phagocytosis, and Ab-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), using target cells infected with DENV or transfected to express DENV-derived surface-bound NS1 protein.
analysis.main_results: Infected subjects generated DENV-4-specific complement-fixing Abs and anti-NS1 Abs that facilitated monocyte-mediated phagocytosis of target cells, and DENV-4-specific Abs also mediated NK cell activation in a subset of subjects.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors demonstrated that non-neutralizing antibodies play a role in immune responses to DENV-4 infection, providing new insights into immune defense beyond neutralizing antibodies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform future research on how nNAbs correlate with disease protection or risk, potentially improving vaccine development and understanding of dengue immunity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its small sample size and focus on a single serotype, but the use of direct measurements of functional antibody responses provides moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized non-neutralizing antibody responses in a DENV-4 human challenge model. In a phase 1 open-label study, 14 dengue-naïve subjects were inoculated with a live attenuated DENV-4 strain. Plasma was analyzed for Ab-dependent complement deposition, phagocytosis, and cytotoxicity using DENV-infected or NS1-expressing target cells. Results showed DENV-4-specific complement-fixing Abs, anti-NS1 Abs facilitating monocyte phagocytosis, and NK cell activation in some subjects. The study highlights the role of nNAbs in dengue immunity, with future work planned to extend findings to tetravalent vaccine recipients. The evidence strength is moderate, limited by sample size and single-serotype focus.

title: Unmanaged plastic waste significantly increases dengue burden

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The material-specific surveillance framework offers a practical indicator for both downstream vector surveillance and upstream waste-management and plastic policies, directly informing public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on observational surveillance data and a novel index, though the nationwide scope and empirical approach provide robust support for the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of plastic pollution in dengue transmission by developing a material-specific extension of the Breteau Index for Aedes larval surveillance in Sri Lanka. The research found that discarded non-biodegradable waste, particularly plastic containers, serves as a major breeding habitat, accounting for 30–34% of national dengue burden and 22–23% in sentinel districts. The material-partitioning approach provides a novel surveillance framework that quantifies the link between unmanaged waste and dengue risk, offering practical tools for vector control and waste management policies. While observational in nature, the nationwide data and empirical methods support the conclusion that plastic pollution significantly contributes to dengue transmission.

title: Molecular detection of Coxiella burnetii in suspected dengue patients from the Bauru region, São Paulo State, Brazil.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the molecular detection of Coxiella burnetii in serum samples from patients with suspected dengue fever in São Paulo State, Brazil. Over 300 samples were collected over three years, and all tested negative for dengue, leptospirosis, and brucellosis. Coxiella burnetii DNA was detected in 1.3% of the samples, indicating recent infection. The findings suggest that Q fever should be included in the differential diagnosis of febrile illnesses, emphasizing the need for improved surveillance strategies. However, the study's limited geographic scope and small sample size may affect the generalizability of the results, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between NS1 antigen positivity, dengue virus serotypes, and infection status in 65 RT-PCR-confirmed dengue patients. title: The methodological quality of dengue clinical practice guidelines globally. A systematic review.

analysis.scope_and_question: This study aimed to systematically review the methodological quality of dengue clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) available globally.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review included CPGs on dengue clinical management (clinical diagnosis, investigation and treatment), and the development process of the guidelines, required to be evidence-based and including an expert review process. An electronic search was performed using Google, Google Scholar and PubMed. The search was last performed in September 2025. No language restriction was imposed. The selection of CPGs and cross-checking of data extracted were performed by two independent reviewers with a third to resolve any discrepancies. The Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE-II) was used to assess the quality of CPGs by four independent reviewers.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Despite the variability in the quality of the CPGs assessed in this review, several high-quality guidelines were identified as suitable for use. Among these six CPGs, only three reported the recommendations with GRADE. Majority of the CPGs fail to demonstrate a robust scientific development process.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Four CPGs adapted other CPGs without transparent review process. In contrast, a number of CPGs were found to rely heavily on adaptations of existing guidelines while lacking sufficient methodological rigour.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Therefore, CPGs that adapt recommendations from other sources should still undertake a full and systematic development process consistent with the AGREE II framework.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review assessed the methodological quality of dengue clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) globally. The study included 29 CPGs from 18 countries published between 2009-2025, evaluated using the AGREE-II framework. Six CPGs were rated as high quality, but only three reported recommendations with GRADE. Many guidelines failed to demonstrate a robust scientific development process, and four adapted other guidelines without transparent review. The review identified both high-quality guidelines suitable for use and those lacking methodological rigor, emphasizing the need for systematic development processes even when adapting existing guidelines.

title: Hubungan Perilaku Masyarakat dan Peran Kader dengan Kejadian Demam Berdarah Dengue

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Community preventive behavior and the role of health cadres are significantly associated with the incidence of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever. The findings highlight the importance of community engagement and cadre involvement in dengue prevention efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study underscores the need to strengthen community-based dengue prevention programs and enhance the role of health cadres in vector control to reduce dengue incidence. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the relationship between community behavior, the role of health cadres, and dengue incidence in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia. Using a cross-sectional design with 81 respondents, the study found that most participants had moderate dengue prevention behavior (63.0%) and perceived health cadres as good (58.0%). Statistical analysis revealed significant associations between both community preventive behavior and cadre roles with dengue incidence (p < 0.05). Respondents with good behavior and positive cadre perceptions were less likely to be infected. The findings emphasize the importance of community engagement and cadre involvement in dengue prevention, suggesting targeted interventions could reduce incidence. However, the study's generalizability is limited by its single-site focus and small sample size.

title: Extensive intraventricular hemorrhage, complicated by dengue-induced coagulopathy, initially misdiagnosed as gastroenteritis in a toddler: A case report

analysis.research_question_and_background: Incomplete physical examinations, especially omissions of Central nervous system (CNS) assessments, remain a major cause of missed or delayed diagnoses of serious neurological conditions in febrile children with nonspecific symptoms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: I report the case of a 22-month-old male initially presenting with prolonged fever, coffee-ground vomiting, nonbloody diarrhea, and recurrent convulsions, leading to a presumptive diagnosis of gastroenteritis with sepsis at Mwananyamala regional referral hospital.
analysis.methods: Subsequent evaluation at Muhimbili National Hospital revealed focal neurological deficits, hepatomegaly with jaundice, and severe coagulopathy. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated extensive intraventricular hemorrhage with obstructive hydrocephalus and multifocal acute cerebral infarcts in the setting of severe dengue-associated coagulopathy.
analysis.main_results: Although an underlying vascular malformation was considered, vascular imaging was not performed and this remained unconfirmed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This case highlights the critical diagnostic challenge in pediatric care where common gastrointestinal symptoms can mask severe systemic and neurological conditions, particularly in dengue-endemic areas.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: It highlights the urgent need for high suspicion of central nervous system pathology, comprehensive neurological examinations, and early neuroimaging in children presenting with persistent nonspecific symptoms and new-onset seizures, crucial for timely diagnosis and management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate as this is a single case report, which limits generalizability, but the detailed clinical and imaging findings provide valuable insights into the diagnostic challenges of dengue-induced neurological complications.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 22-month-old male initially misdiagnosed with gastroenteritis and sepsis due to nonspecific symptoms like fever, vomiting, and diarrhea. Subsequent evaluation revealed severe dengue-induced coagulopathy, extensive intraventricular hemorrhage, and cerebral infarcts on MRI. The case underscores the diagnostic challenges in pediatric dengue, where gastrointestinal symptoms can mask severe neurological complications. It emphasizes the need for high suspicion of CNS pathology, comprehensive neurological exams, and early neuroimaging in endemic areas to prevent delayed diagnosis and improve outcomes.

title: IgA Dengue Virus NS1 Immune Complexes Are Associated with In Vitro Neutrophil Activation 2308886

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of circulating IgA targeting non-structural protein 1 (NS1) in modulating neutrophil activation during dengue virus infection, addressing a knowledge gap in the poorly understood contribution of IgA immune complexes to dengue immunopathogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used serum samples from DENV-seropositive individuals in Puerto Rico (n = 20) and neutrophils isolated from healthy donors to evaluate IgA and IgG recognition of recombinant DENV-2 NS1 and envelope proteins and assess neutrophil activation.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were evaluated for IgA and IgG recognition of recombinant DENV-2 NS1 and envelope proteins by ELISA, neutrophils were stimulated with IgA-NS1 or IgG-NS1 immune complexes for 6 hours, and NETosis was quantified using the Incucyte live cell imaging system with correlation analyses performed in GraphPad Prism.
analysis.main_results: IgA favored the recognition of NS1 over E protein (mean NS1/E ratio 1.71) compared to IgG (mean NS1/E ratio 1.09), and NETosis demonstrated a stronger association with IgA-NS1 immune complexes (R2 = 0.42, p < 0.0001) than with IgG-NS1 complexes (R2 = 0.15, p = 0.026).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that IgA-NS1 immune complexes may serve as potential modulators of neutrophil-driven inflammation in dengue, representing a distinct immunopathogenic pathway particularly relevant during heterologous DENV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest a novel mechanism for dengue immunopathogenesis that could inform future surveillance, diagnostic strategies, and therapeutic interventions targeting IgA-NS1 interactions to mitigate neutrophil-mediated inflammation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the small sample size (n = 20) and reliance on in vitro neutrophil stimulation, which may not fully recapitulate in vivo conditions; however, the statistical significance of the findings supports the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the role of IgA targeting dengue virus non-structural protein 1 (NS1) in neutrophil activation. Using serum from DENV-seropositive individuals and neutrophils from healthy donors, the researchers found that IgA preferentially recognized NS1 over envelope protein compared to IgG. IgA-NS1 immune complexes induced significantly stronger neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation than IgG-NS1 complexes, suggesting a distinct immunopathogenic pathway in dengue. These findings highlight a potential mechanism for neutrophil-driven inflammation during heterologous DENV infection, warranting further investigation into therapeutic targeting of IgA-NS1 interactions.

title: A Multiplex RT-LAMP-Lateral Flow Platform For Comprehensive Dengue Serotype Detection

The platform is proposed to enhance early diagnosis and surveillance in resource-limited settings, though clinical validation and comparative performance data are not reported.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid IgM cross-reactivity among arboviruses in Japanese encephalitis patients from southern India.
